THE MEMORY WAS THE MEDIUM

A program with a physical address.

Core-rope memory encoded the fixed program and constants through the routing of wires relative to magnetic cores. The computer also had erasable magnetic-core memory for changing state.

36,864fixed words
2,048erasable words

The relevant Apollo word contained 15 information bits and a parity bit. “72 KB” is convenient shorthand using sixteen-bit storage words; it does not describe a modern byte-addressed machine.

Rope storage constrained deployment. It did not abolish software: source still had to be designed, assembled, tested and turned into an executable representation.

THE EXECUTIVE HAD PRIORITIES

Save the landing. Lose the queue.

The real Executive scheduled jobs by priority. Restart protection let essential calculations resume from registered points; expendable work could disappear during recovery.

1202 meant there was no free core set to schedule a job. 1201 meant there was no free vector-accumulator area. These were resource-exhaustion alarms, not arbitrary “CPU over 100%” indicators.

This lab uses a simple workload budget to expose the trade-off. Its alarm thresholds, timings and shedding amounts are invented teaching parameters. They are not measurements of the Apollo Executive.

SCEPTICISM YOU CAN TEST

Three different questions.

  1. Is the code authentic? Compare the transcription with scanned listings and independently checked octal words and bank checksums.
  2. Can it perform the guidance task? Execute the right program in a validated emulator, with physical dynamics, sensors and initial conditions.
  3. Did the reported flight happen? That requires the broader historical record. A successful simulation alone cannot establish a past event.

Virtual AGC documents both validation and version identification. “Luminary 99” is a useful family name; selecting the actual flight branch matters.

Virtual AGC: provenance & validation ↗
WHAT THIS FIRST BUILD DOES

Make the constraints playable.

Two-dimensional near-surface motion, constant lunar gravity (1.62 m/s²), fuel-dependent mass, a throttled and tilted engine, and a modern automatic controller. The flat landing pad, 600 m starting height, safety limits and all workload units are experiment design choices.

It omits orbital navigation, rotating reference frames, terrain elevation, sensor noise, actuator delays, the actual AGC instruction set and the historical P63/P64/P66 equations. Program numbers are illustrative phase labels.

Next: integrate an established AGC core, pin the flight binary, validate instruction behaviour, then couple sensors and vehicle dynamics. Compare nominal runs, overload and engine-delay faults against documented results.
